entry.p: Driven by thermal concerns (need sufficient load on TIM to achieve adequate thermal performance)

row.entry: Driven by Intel package mechanical limits

Things to consider:
Appropriate selection of TIM (customer choice)
Relationship between pressure and thermal resistance/ impedance for the selected TIM
Force required to provide the needed total average TIM pressure, based on die area (customer calculation, refer to the ).
Cross-reference Intel's assumed Technical Targets for TIM resistance (refer to the ).
Avoid heatsink contact with package stiffener, which reduces force on TIM and may impact thermal performance.

Things to consider:
Total allowable force on package, which depends on the specific Intel package plus several customer choices including PCB thickness, use of a backplate, and use of corner glue (refer to the ).
Allowable peak pressure on any 2mm x 2mm area of the die. This applies for both “static pressure” (i.e., steady-state), and “transient pressure” (i.e., occurring very briefly during the heatsink attachment process) (refer to the ).
Refer to the #575675 for guidance on using structural simulation to check heatsink conformance to load and pressure specifications.
Refer to the #556532 for a recommended method for measuring heatsink pressure on each 2mm x 2mm area of the die using a commercial thin film pressure sensor.
